answer: Each agent identity must post a stake per epoch before its work is scored, and payouts unlock only after auditors confirm the prior epoch. A Sybil farm therefore keeps every fake funded across the delay, unable to recycle earnings into the next batch. The anchor is a margin scaling with identities sharing an operator graph: more fakes demand more locked capital before any reward clears. An oasis opens for the lone honest agent paying little, while a farm pays per seat until margins die. No spiral of refunds helps, since duplicate-claim detection forfeits stakes. Cost grows with fakes.
